messages.subject: Specific axis labels bolded
parts:
Hello all,

I have data set like the one below where I have data points plotted and dodged as there are multiple points per sampling data. I was wondering if anyone could suggest any way that I might be able to either change the colour of or bold the sampling date axis label to better distinguish it from all the non-sampling dates? The example below should illustrate what type of plot I am dealing with and where I was hoping to have the axis label bolded.

Thanks in advance!

Sam

library(ggplot2)
dat <- data.frame(x = runif(12, 0, 125), date = as.Date(c("2009-09-25","2009-09-28","2009-10-02","2009-10-07","2009-10-15","2009-10-21"), format="%Y-%m-%d"), yy = letters[1:2], stringsAsFactors = TRUE)



pl <- ggplot(dat) +
  geom_point(aes(date, x, colour=yy), size = 4, position = position_dodge(width = 2)) +
  theme_bw() +
  #facet_wrap(~sed.type, ncol=1, scales="free_y") +
  scale_x_date(major = "1 day") +
  opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=45, hjust=1, vjust=1), strip.text.x = theme_text(size = 16))
pl

messages.subject: Re: Specific axis labels bolded
parts:
I've done this before with factor levels, just feed the axis text option with a string of colors. 

opts(title="Iceberg - Postharvest Quality"

,strip.background = theme_rect(colour = 'NA', fill = 'NA')

,axis.text.y = theme_text(colour=c("red", "black", "red", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "red", "black", "red", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "black", "red", "black", "black", "black", "black", "red"), hjust=1))


I've never tried it with dates, but if your dates are evenly spaced you could always treat them like factors and do the above. If not, (..shudder..). 


Brandon
